t19: The most asked question about backgammon is not a rule, it's setup: which piece goes where? The arrangement is actually a single pattern and once you learn it, you never forget it. It's below with a diagram.
t21: The backgammon board has 24 points (triangles); the divider in the middle is called the
t23: and splits the board in two. Each player has 15 pieces.
t24: Points are numbered 1 to 24 in each player's direction. Your point 1 is your opponent's point 24; so the two players move in opposite directions.
t26: Each player's 15 pieces are gathered on four points. The pattern is:
t28: — on point 24 (the farthest corner, opponent's home board)
t37: Starting setup. White and black use the same pattern mirrored; each player moves in their own direction.
t38: Your opponent's setup is a mirror of the same pattern
t39: Your opponent uses exactly the same numbers, just in their direction. This is why when you look at the board the setup looks symmetric: pairs of pieces in opposite corners, groups of five and three in the middle.
t40: Practical check: on a correctly set board, each point has either 2, 3, or 5 pieces; any other number means there's an error somewhere.
t42: Each player moves from their own point 24 toward point 1, which means the numbers decrease. Your home board is points 1–6; once you've gathered all your pieces there, you start bearing them off (taking them off the board).
t43: Because the two players move in opposite directions, their pieces pass through each other — all the game's tension comes from this.
t45: Putting the stack of 5 on the wrong point.
t46: Points 6 and 13 each have five pieces; putting them on 12 is a common mix-up.
t48: Your home board is 1–6; you move toward it, not away from it.
t49: Putting the pair of pieces on the wrong corner.
t50: The pair of pieces is on the farthest corner, not the closest to you.
t52: Each player must have exactly 15 pieces; having too few or too many is discovered mid-game.
t54: When setup is complete, each player rolls one die; the higher roll starts and uses both dice for the first move. If the rolls are equal, the dice are rolled again.

t60: Which direction do you move in backgammon?
t61: Each player moves from their point 24 toward point 1. Your home board is points 1–6; the two players move in opposite directions.
t62: How do I know the setup is correct?
t63: On a correctly set board, every filled point has only 2, 3, or 5 pieces, and each player has 15 total pieces. If you see any other number, the setup is wrong.
